tickets.title: FraudScore 0.77 on inbound wire to wealth account - counterparty review
tickets.description: FraudScore flagged transaction t_000194, an inbound wire of $6,762.17 received 2026-07-03 into {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00356}} for {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0172}} (wealth). Score 0.77, which is above our manual review threshold of 0.70. The originator is Giles, Johnson and Adams, which is a first-time counterparty on this account. Alert surfaced in the queue on 2026-07-21 after the batch re-score. Requesting analyst triage: confirm source of funds, check counterparty against prior activity, and decide whether escalation to AML is needed.

comments.text: Pulled the wire details. Originator is a professional services firm and the remittance reference matches an invoice settlement the advisor documented in ClientHub in June. Amount is in line with prior inflows on the account.

Sanctions screen on originator and originating bank came back clean. Score was driven by new-counterparty and round-ish timing features, not by anything behavioral. Marking false positive, no SAR referral.
Thanks Anthony. Closing. Please note the counterparty in the review log so a repeat from the same originator doesn't get re-triaged.

tickets.title: Repeat FraudScore alert on same originator, new-counterparty feature suspected
tickets.description: A second FraudScore alert fired on 2026-07-22 tied to the same inbound wire activity on {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00356}} belonging to {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0172}}. Reference transaction is t_000194 ($6,762.17, wire_in, 2026-07-03, score 0.77) from Giles, Johnson and Adams. This looks like the nightly re-score regenerating an alert after yesterday's review. Need to confirm whether this is a duplicate of the earlier triage or a new signal, and whether the alert suppression for reviewed transactions is functioning.

comments.text: Confirmed duplicate. The re-score job emitted a new alert id because the model version tag changed during last night's deploy, so the dedupe key didn't match the already-dispositioned alert.
Agreed, no new risk signal. Underlying review from yesterday stands as false positive. Thanks for tracing the dedupe issue.
I'll fix the dedupe key to exclude the model version tag. Leaving this resolved; change goes out with the next FraudScore release.

tickets.title: Retrospective review of FraudScore 0.77 alert on wire from known professional services originator
tickets.description: Quarterly QA sampling of dispositioned FraudScore alerts selected t_000194, an inbound wire of $6,762.17 on 2026-07-03 to {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00356}} for {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0172}}. Original score was 0.77 with a false positive disposition. QA task on 2026-08-13: re-verify that the documented rationale holds up, confirm supporting evidence is attached, and check that no later activity on the account changes the picture, such as outbound movement of the funds shortly after receipt.

comments.text: Reviewed the file. Invoice reference and advisor note are attached. No rapid outbound movement after receipt; the funds stayed in the account and were allocated per the client's standing investment plan.
Disposition as false positive is supported. Only gap was a missing screenshot of the sanctions result, which I've added to the case record.

tickets.title: FraudScore threshold tuning check after alert on wealth inbound wire
tickets.description: On 2026-10-02 an alert was raised against {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00356}} ({{CLIENT_NAME:c_0172}}) referencing transaction t_000194, wire_in $6,762.17 from Giles, Johnson and Adams, score 0.77. The transaction dates to 2026-07-03 and was previously cleared, so this appears to be an alert generated by a back-fill after the model retrain. Please confirm it is a false positive tied to the earlier review and note whether the retrained model still scores this pattern high enough to be worth tuning.

comments.text: Matched to the July disposition. The counterparty has since sent two more wires on the same invoice cycle and none were flagged at that level, so the history supports legitimacy.

The back-fill ran with the retrained model against 90 days of history, which explains the stale alert. I'll share the feature contributions with Nadia so we can decide whether the counterparty-age weight needs adjusting.
Good, thanks both. Resolving as false positive; I'll follow up on the weighting separately.

tickets.title: FraudScore alert reappearing on cleared wire - confirm no new activity on wealth account
tickets.description: Another FraudScore hit on 2026-10-13 mentions transaction t_000194 ($6,762.17 inbound wire dated 2026-07-03, score 0.77) for {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0172}} at {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00356}}. This transaction was already dispositioned as a false positive in July and was sampled in the August QA review. Need someone to verify whether the alert is another stale re-surface or if it is linked to any new inbound or outbound activity on the account, and to close it with a note if nothing new is found.

comments.text: Checked account activity since 2026-10-01. Only routine dividend credits and the scheduled advisory fee debit. Nothing tied to the originator in the alert. Leaning toward stale re-surface again.
Makes sense. Can you confirm with Jenna whether the dedupe fix from July is live in production before we close? If it is, this shouldn't have regenerated.
